Chapter 9: Sustaining Confidence Through Life’s Storms
Let’s be honest—confidence isn’t something you find once and keep forever, untouched by life. We all face storms: illness, loss, disappointment. No one gets a free pass. The real question isn’t whether hard times will come, but how you can hold onto enough when they do.
Picture this: a woman who’s been making steady progress suddenly loses her job. Out of nowhere, all those old fears creep back in. Maybe she was never really good enough. It’s so tempting to fall into that spiral of self-doubt. But then, she remembers what’s helped her in the past—reaching out to friends, leaning into her faith, and coming back to the truths she’s learned about herself. The storm doesn’t pass overnight. But this time, she weathers it with more resilience than she ever thought possible.
Or think about someone facing a health crisis that changes everything—the plans she’d made, the identity she’d built, all of it seems to fall apart. In the middle of that uncertainty, she discovers a new kind of confidence. Not the kind built on achievements or how she looks, but on the unshakeable truth of her worth. She learns it’s okay to ask for help, to rest when she needs to, and to trust that she is enough—even when she can’t do all the things she used to do.
The truth is, most of us find our confidence gets tested during the toughest seasons. The old lies can feel even louder. Those stories we thought we’d outgrown? They can come rushing back. But here’s the thing—these moments also show us what’s real. The practices of enough—being in community, letting ourselves be vulnerable, telling the truth—those become our lifelines.
The storms? They don’t define you. They reveal the strength that’s been growing inside you all along.
